learning_outcomes.text: To teach students, mainly through laboratory experience, the fundamental concepts of bioelectronics, understood as a discipline that applies the principles and technologies of electronics to biology, medicine, and life sciences.

To provide students with the tools necessary for the analysis, design, and characterization of bioelectronic devices, and more specifically biosensors, for application in the medical and healthcare sectors.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to bioelectronics: Introduction to bioelectronics and bioelectronic devices for diagnostics (sensors) and therapy (actuators).
Biosensors for measuring chemical, physical, and physiological parameters of clinical interest.
Overview of biological recognition elements, labeled and label-free approaches.
Transduction mechanisms and principles, with particular attention to those of an electrochemical and optical nature.
Properties of biosensors (sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility, stability, linearity, etc.) and evaluation of performance and technical limitations.
Commercial, regulatory, ethical, and practical obstacles in the development of bioelectronic devices in the medical and healthcare fields.

Laboratory exercises on biosensors. At least four laboratory exercises will be carried out aimed at the analysis and characterization of different types of biosensors based on electrochemical and optical transduction mechanisms.

Study of a scientific paper: The teacher assigns students a scientific paper from an international journal related to a topic covered in the course, which they critically examine and discuss with their classmates through a presentation or poster.

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of technical reports (slides showing the main results achieved) prepared as a group at the end of each lab exercise

assessment_rules: The oral exam assesses knowledge of topics and exercises. To pass, students must demonstrate knowledge of transduction principles and configurations of bioelectronic devices, understanding their performance and technical limitations. Technical reports from lab exercises will be commented on during the oral exam.
bibliography: "Introductory Bioelectronics: for Engineers and Physical Scientists", R. Pethig and S. Smith, Wiley, 2012, ISBN: 978-1119970873 lecture notes files which will be shared regularly throughout the course.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica E Biomedica (Electronics And Biomedical Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
